figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1. Chemical space of products downstream of the diterpenes and diterpene 
acids. A, Level (I) in the center represents the universal precursor GGPP, Level 
(II) represents the published products of the bifunctional diTPS (left semi-circle) 
and class I diTPS (right semi-circle, together with a (+)CPS enzyme. The size of 
the sectors is proportional to the numbers products generated by DiTPS. DiTPS 
that were selected for this study use either GGPP (left side) or (+)-CPP (right 
side) as substrate to produce the diterpene skeletons shown belonging to either 
abietane, pimarane, or labdane backbone type. They serve as substrates for 
RoCYP76AH22 (blue), OsCYP76M8 (red), SpCYP71BE52 (green) and 
PsCYP720B4 (yellow) for oxidation at C2, C6, C7, C9, C11, C12 and C18. The 
published oxidation sites are highlighted with asterisks in the colour matching 
the oxidating CYP; asterisks in brackets refer to oxidations by OsCYP76M8 on 
substrates of syn- or ent-configuration. B, Sunburst plot of products resulting 
from the combination of 1 CYP with 1 diTPS (level III) (first level with colours) 
or 2 CYPs with 1 diTPS (level IV; outermost level). The size of the sectors is 
proportional to the number of products identified. Colours represent the CYP 
involved in the formation of the product (RoCYP76AH22 (blue), OsCYP76M8 
(red), SpCYP71BE52 (green) and PsCYP720B4 (yellow)). In the outer circle the 
total circumference represents 217 diterpenes. Some of the main products are 
shown with their position in the sunburst and their structure elucidated 
by NMR.

figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 5. Comparison of catalytic competent docking pose of nezukol and trans-biformene showing the catalytic orientation of substrates in PsCYP720B4 for selective 
oxidation at 18 and 3 positions. A Trans-biformene C18–H indicated with cyan and βC3-H in red are closer to compound I oxygen in terms of catalytic distance 
suggesting the oxidation will be reactive towards both positions C18 and βC3. B Nezukol C18–H indicated with cyan is closer to compound I oxygen than C3–H, thus 
the selective oxidation will be more reactive to position C18.
